# `aitbc messaging dm keygen`

Create (or rotate) this wallet's DM key and publish the public half on-chain. DRY RUN by default. With --confirm: a new X25519 keypair is stored in the mode-600 dm-keys file and a ``dm_key`` envelope is signed and submitted.

## Usage

```bash
aitbc messaging dm keygen [OPTIONS]
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--wallet` | text | — | yes | Wallet that signs the dm_key publication |
| `--fee` | decimal | `0.01` | no | Transaction fee (AIT) |
| `--confirm` | flag | `false` | no | Generate the key (if needed) and sign+submit once (default: dry run) |
| `--rotate` | flag | `false` | no | Publish a fresh key even if one exists (old eras are kept in the key file for old ciphertext) |
| `--rpc-url` | text | — | no | Blockchain RPC URL |
| `--password-stdin` | flag | `false` | no | Read the wallet password from one line of standard input |
| `--password-file` | file | — | no | Path to a file containing only the wallet password (mode 0600, owned by you) |
| `--password` | text | — | no | Wallet password (deprecated: visible in process lists and shell history; prefer --password-stdin or --password-file) |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc messaging dm keygen --wallet <wallet_name>
RPC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8202/rpc
aitbc messaging dm keygen --wallet <wallet_name> --rpc-url "$RPC_URL"
```
